summary.text: Mike McGuire is a Democratic California State Senator who first won public office at age 19 on the Healdsburg School Board, later serving on the Healdsburg City Council and Sonoma County Board of Supervisors before his 2014 election to the State Senate. He served as Senate Majority Leader and then as President pro Tempore from 2024 to 2025. He announced his run for Congress in November 2025 and advanced from the June 2, 2026 primary.

paragraphs.text: McGuire was born in Healdsburg, California, in 1979 and earned a B.A. in political science from Sonoma State University in 2002. He worked in the radio and television industries.

He was first elected to public office in 1998, at age 19, to the Healdsburg School Board, and was elected to the Healdsburg City Council in 2004. In 2010 he was elected to the Sonoma County Board of Supervisors.

McGuire was elected to the California State Senate in 2014, defeating Republican Lawrence R. Wiesner 70%-30%, and was re-elected in 2018 and 2022 with more than 66% of the vote each time. He represents District 2, which covers Marin, Sonoma, Lake, Mendocino, Humboldt, Trinity and Del Norte counties.

Then-President pro Tempore Toni Atkins selected him as Senate Majority Leader in January 2022, and he was elected Senate President pro Tempore on February 5, 2024. Ballotpedia reports he was the first senator from California's northern coast chosen to lead the Senate since 1866.
In June 2025 McGuire agreed to step down as Senate leader so S. Monique Limon could succeed him, and he left the position on November 17, 2025. He announced his congressional campaign the same month.
The Associated Press, as quoted by Ballotpedia, reported that he authored legislation on marine life, cannabis farmers, cellphone service during power outages, and wildfire impacts.

sources.title: State Senate leader McGuire launches bid for Congress, challenging LaMalfa
